content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a full source ledger before reporting.

input.summary:
Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (the truncated restatement ending "To remove the clamp, releasing"); input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority and no-government-support formalities, and the drafting agent's "YOU" turn (which asserts an unrelated "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface") was treated as context only and correctly appears nowhere in the draft.

CLAIMS: every limitation of claims 1-17 was traced. Claim 1 (frame halves/hinge end/latch end, three circumferentially distributed jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads, carriage springs biasing outward, cam ring in annular guide rotating through a limited stroke, first/second cam-ring segments carried one per frame half, complementary drive faces at the hinge end and latch end coupling on closure, follower in oblique slot inclined to the circumferential direction, wedge on the latch bearing on a ring drive face, force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge) maps sentence-for-sentence onto disclosure paragraphs 1-3. Claims 2-3 trace to "additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others"; claim 4 and 12 and 15 to "A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range"; claim 5 to the first/over-center position sentence; claim 6 to "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages" read with "rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others"; claim 7 and 16 to "One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half" plus the removal paragraph; claims 8, 13 and 17 to "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit"; claims 9-10 to the carriage-spring and tool-specific-diameter sentences; claim 11 (installed assembly) and claim 14 (method) to the clamped-on-pipe and install/remove paragraphs. No means-plus-function language, three independent claims, correct antecedent basis chains (claim 2 introduces "a pipe", claim 3 uses "the pipe").

NUMERALS: all 28 entries (10-66, with 28 unused) were checked one-for-one against the description; each designates exactly one part, each is used in the description, and each appears on at least one sheet. Segment/face assignments are internally consistent across views: FIG. 1 fixes 12 upper / 14 lower and hinge 16 at the left break with latch 18 at the right; FIG. 3 places 32 upper / 34 lower and 44/46 at the left (hinge-end) junction and 48/50 at the right (latch-end) junction, matching "first hinge-end drive face 44 ... first latch-end drive face 48" on segment 32 and 46/50 on segment 34.

FIGURE BRIEFS AND DRAWING DESCRIPTION: the four briefs match draft/07-drawings.md view-for-view and numeral-for-numeral. Geometry choices were tested against the functional-surface rule. The generic outlines that are called schematic (hinge, latch body, housing, wedge block, spring column, indicator rod, boss pad, band and channel arcs, abutting segment end faces of "matching outline") assert no taper, angle, depth, runout, proportion or material, and the descriptive text and claims stay shape-neutral; no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening statement was introduced into the application text to justify a renderer choice. Substantive statements that do appear are traced: the concave pad edge contacting the pipe and not the carriage ("carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe"); slots sharing one rotational sense and equal angular spacing ("oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"); segment junctions at the frame breaks and the annular guide divided there ("One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half"); the ring drive face at the latch-end junction, which is forced by "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring" with the latch at the latch end; the spring stack lying between handle and wedge in FIG. 4 ("A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge"); and the boss projection radially outboard of the channel ("outside the annular guide"). The FIG. 1 lever ("outward and downward to the right") and the FIG. 4 lever ("upward and to the right") reconcile exactly under the stated 90-degree turn of the FIG. 4 view. No section lines are designated in any view, so no repeated section designation is required. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any application section; the depiction conventions are confined to the figure briefs.

One minor issue is reported: the mounting boss is drawn in FIG. 2 but deliberately left unnumbered even though the description ties 66 to annular guide 36 in the FIG. 2 discussion. No unsupported technical assertion, claim-scope excess, or terminology conflict was found.

findings.title: Mounting boss is drawn in FIG. 2 but left unnumbered, although the description states its relationship to annular guide 36 in the FIG. 2 discussion and three claims recite that relationship
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (front-matter numerals list, last bullet of "Geometry to draw", "Numeral placement targets"); draft/07-drawings.md (FIG. 2 sentence); draft/08-detailed-description.md ("The segmented cam ring" section)
findings.detail: FIG. 2 is the only view that shows the annular guide (channel 36), and its brief draws the mounting boss there but expressly withholds the numeral. The description asserts the boss/guide relationship inside the FIG. 2 discussion ("The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36."), and claims 8, 13 and 17 recite the boss "outside the annular guide," yet no single sheet carries both 66 and 36, so the recited relationship is nowhere identified by reference characters. This is an internal labelling inconsistency only: the boss and its position outside the annular guide are affirmatively disclosed ("The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit."), and the projection is already drawn in the correct place, so numbering it introduces no new technical matter and no new geometry.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md geometry: "An unnumbered small rectangular projection standing radially outward on the outer boundary circle at the upper right, radially outboard of the channel." FIG-2.md front matter: "numerals: [22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42]" (66 absent). Description: "The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36." Claim 8: "wherein the frame carries a mounting boss outside the annular guide." Disclosure: "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md: change the front matter to "numerals: [22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42, 66]"; change the geometry bullet to "A small rectangular projection standing radially outward on the outer boundary circle at the upper right, radially outboard of the channel."; change the numerals line to "Reference numerals appearing on this sheet: 22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42, 66."; add the placement target "- 66: well inside the small rectangular projection at the upper right."; add "66" to the "## Numerals shown on this figure" list; and add the projection to the schematic sentence so it reads "The band, the channel, the followers, the springs and the small rectangular projection are shown schematically." In draft/07-drawings.md, end the FIG. 2 sentence "... the jaw pads, the carriage springs and the mounting boss outside the annular guide." Make no change to draft/08-detailed-description.md or to the claims.
